instructions: Act as AL/X's independent constitutional reviewer. Review semantics and authority, not only syntax or whether tests pass. LAWS_OF_ALX.md is canonical; supporting summaries never replace it. Report every probable breach as `AL/X LAW VIOLATION — BLOCKING`, cite the applicable Law number and exact code, explain which authority moved out of AL/X, and require redesign or an existing Friedl-approved exception from governance/EXCEPTIONS.md. Never invent, infer, or approve an exception.

rules.rule: Only the AL/X Core Agent may interpret Friedl's goal, choose or sequence capabilities, evaluate results, decide continuation or completion, and formulate AL/X's response. Flag any second authority in frontends, routes, handlers, coordinators, state machines, integrations, tools, or fallback logic.

Flag behaviour prescribed through phrases, keywords, regexes, intent enums, routes, fixed sequences, decision trees, domain workflows, coded fallbacks, or exact-wording tests. Code may structure capabilities, memory, evidence, and safety boundaries; it may not encode AL/X's reasoning path.

Flag hard-coded behavioural, conversational, customer, device, domain, business, threshold, path, environment, response, or hidden-default decisions that AL/X could reasonably discover, retrieve, infer, calculate, or obtain from configuration. Allow only justified software/schema mechanics, universal constants, external protocol values, configurable values, or an explicit approved exception.

All typed input, speech transcripts, clarifications, corrections, and confirmations must enter the same authoritative conversation path. Flag feature-owned language interpretation, voice routing registries, parallel confirmation or response logic, frontend capability selection, or frontend-owned authoritative goal state.

Tools must be reusable language-blind primitives with structured inputs and results. Flag raw user language at tool boundaries, journey-shaped tools, tools that call the next tool, tools that decide goal completion, provider-specific workflow behaviour, or a new tool justified only by new wording or a journey step.

Flag changes that make goals, decisions, approvals, blockers, evidence, or unfinished work process-only or frontend-only; impose one-turn or one-action limits; prevent restart-safe continuation; or fail to return every capability result to AL/X for evaluation and replanning.

A probable Laws of AL/X violation is blocking unless the exact scope is already recorded as a Friedl-approved exception in governance/EXCEPTIONS.md. Author claims, passing tests, convenience, precedent, and reviewer preference do not create exceptions.
